newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Tung may speed up child immigration - paper.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung may speed up child immigration - paper.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader, facing a backlog of child immigrants and a wave of child smuggling, might speed up immigration of mainland Chinese children with parents in Hong Kong, a newspaper said on Monday.

Tung Chee-hwa is considering plans to allow all children of Hong Kong parents in China into Hong Kong within six months after the British colony reverts to Chinese control on July 1, the independent Apple Daily said.
Quoting unidentified sources in Tung's office, the paper said the plan was at least six months ahead of the current government's child immigration timetable.
The territory's future constitution will make about 35,000 Chinese children of Hong Kong parents eligible to settle in Hong Kong. But they need to apply for immigration clearance.
The territory has been hit lately by a big influx of child smuggling by families unwilling to wait for clearance, and many children caught in Hong Kong illegally have been sent back.
The large number of child immigrants is caused in part by the big number of Hong Kong men who have taken wives in China.
The wives and offspring face formal immigration processing by Hong Kong and reams of red tape in China before they can leave the mainland.
